subject: MAP: evaluation acceptance checkpoints, exit conditions, and verification tests
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Lila Shroff <lila.shroff@medsync.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: evaluation acceptance checkpoints, exit conditions, and verification tests

Hi Lila —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I attached a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MedSync_MAP_v1.2.pdf) that turns the high-level goals into concrete acceptance tests, exit gates, and a proposed cutover timeline. The goal here is to make the evaluation deterministic so both teams can track progress and unblock procurement/ops.

Key pieces in the draft:
- Success criteria (functional + non-functional) mapped to test owners
- Exit gates: what winds up the trial early vs. what triggers remediation
- Acceptance tests: smoke tests, concordance checks, latency sampling, and infra failover rehearsals
- Demo/hand-off dates and deliverables for go/no-go decision

Two asks from our side to finalize the plan:
1) Please confirm the top-3 success metrics you need to see to sign off (we suggested concordance >= 92% on sampled transcripts, median inference latency <= 280ms at 99th percentile traffic profile, and no PII leakage incidents in detection runs).
2) Flag any procurement/legal blockers (DocuSign preference, specific audit logging retention).

We also included a short verification matrix (latency-concordance-test-plan.xlsx) that maps test harnesses to responsibilities — Ben (CC'd) will run point on the test harness and Marissa will manage stakeholder demos.

Proposed timeline (high level):
- Week 0: MAP sign-off + sandbox access
- Week 1–2: test harness run & smoke verification
- Week 3: integration demo + sample concordance review
- Week 4: go/no-go decision and procurement handoff

If that lines up, can you confirm by EOD Friday so we can lock the sandbox and schedule test windows?

Regards,

Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MedSync_MAP_v1.2.pdf (PDF, 1 page summary), latency-concordance-test-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Dr. Lila Shroff <lila.shroff@medsync.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medsync.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: evaluation acceptance checkpoints, exit conditions, and verification tests

Rafael —

Thanks for the clear plan and the fast turnaround. Overall this looks good and much more actionable than our usual pilots. A few clarifying notes from the MedSync side:

1) Metrics nuance: concordance thresholds look fine but we need them split by "ED transcripts" and "outpatient notes" because our clinical tolerance differs. For ED transcripts the target should be >= 94%; for outpatient notes we can accept >= 90%.
2) Latency: our primary concern is tail latency during burst loads (e.g., 10 concurrent streams for triage). Can you refine the test to include a 10x-burst profile and report 95th/99th P99 latencies?
3) Security/compliance: procurement asked for confirmation that audit logs and request tracing will be retained for 90 days and made available for our SOC audit. Can your Private offering meet that retention in a sandbox?

Also: for acceptance tests include a small targeted POI/PHI detection run (we'll supply a redacted corpus). If any detection flags, that's a hard blocker until we can validate the remediation path.

Assuming those changes are made we can sign the MAP next week and route the PoV document to procurement. We prefer DocuSign; procurement@medsync.ai will be the signer.

Best,

Lila Shroff, PhD
VP Clinical Informatics
MedSync

Lila —

Really helpful notes, thank you. Confirming actions and updates we will make before final MAP delivery:

- Split concordance targets by transcript type (ED >= 94%, Outpatient >= 90%) and add sampling plan (n=200 ED, n=500 outpatient across runs). Owner: Marissa.
- Add burst profile to latency tests and report 95th/99th percentiles; we'll run the 10-concurrent-stream scenario you described. Owner: Ben.
- Audit logs/retention: we'll provision a sandbox with 90-day retention and provide an export path for your SOC reviewer. This will be called out in the MAP and in the Proc/Legal addendum. Owner: Product Security (we'll loop them in).
- PHI detection run: add a hard-block gate and define remediation SLA (48 hours for triage + 7 days for fix verification). Owner: MedSync + Redwood ops runbook.

Marissa/Ben — please take the owners above and update the attached artifacts today. I want to send the updated MAP to Lila & procurement by Thurs EOD so they can route DocuSign next week.

Lila — one more logistic question: preferred sandbox region? We can provision in us-west (default) or us-east; let us know if you need EU region for data locality.

Thanks,

Rafael
